208.body:
Repeated literature connector failures amplify latency across parallel research agents

Real E2E runs on `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `1a0cb9d5` show a non-fatal but significant research-efficiency problem. Agents eventually deliver reports using alternative sources, but continue querying unavailable/rate-limited connectors across independent branches.

## Observations

The experiment ran four cases concurrently, with native task dispatch and Swarm execution, memory graph disabled, and 24 GiB per case. These are observed counts, not a controlled concurrency experiment.

| Run | arXiv failures | Details | Other academic connector failures |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| DRB-62 repeat 1 | 65 | 60 HTTP 406; 5 slot-wait timeouts | 0 Europe PMC/PubMed |
| DRB-62 repeat 2 | 100 | 30 HTTP 406; 46 HTTP 429; 24 slot-wait timeouts | 14 Europe PMC; 6 PubMed |
| DRB-64 repeat 1 | 59 | All arXiv invocations failed | 2 PubMed |
| DRB-64 repeat 2 | 80 | All arXiv invocations failed | 29 Europe PMC; 3 PubMed |

DRB-62 repeat 2 included agent-issued `sleep 30`, `sleep 90`, and `sleep 150` followed by retries. Connector errors included `HTTP 406 Not Acceptable from export.arxiv.org`, `HTTP 429 Unknown Error from export.arxiv.org`, and `arxiv is rate limited and no slot became free within the wait window`. Some upstream failures were surfaced as `retryable:false`, but later calls to the same source still occurred.

Generation time increased from 18.8 to 69.1 minutes for DRB-62 and from 33.2 to 51.2 minutes for DRB-64. This is **not** an attribution of the whole increase to connectors: expanded research scope, synthesis work, and a separate stream disconnect also contributed.

## Investigation / improvement scope

- Diagnose 406 separately from 429: request/endpoint rejection should not be treated as ordinary rate limiting. Verify the actual upstream requests and responses before choosing a fix.
- Make source cooldown/health visible across sibling agents and, where appropriate, concurrent case workers. Confirm existing rate-limit scope before adding another mechanism.
- Honor Retry-After where available; provide bounded admission waits and explicit retry timing. Avoid multiple agents independently sleeping and repeating requests against a persistently failing source.
- Provide actionable fallback guidance without silently changing scholarly evidence requirements.
- Keep low-volume structured diagnostics: source, sanitized endpoint, status, wait duration, retry decision, request/run correlation IDs; never log credentials.

## Reproduction and acceptance

1. Run DRB-62/64 with parallel literature branches and inspect per-source invocation status plus queue waits. The production upstream failure is intermittent, so this alone is not a deterministic reproducer.
2. Add deterministic connector fault injection for sustained 406, repeated 429 with Retry-After, and slot exhaustion across concurrent callers.
3. Verify failures are reported honestly, repeated requests/waits are bounded, cooldown is shared at the intended scope, recovery occurs after cooldown, and alternative sources remain usable.

Local retained evidence (available on the experiment host): `/root/sciencediscovery-real9-3x-20260926/DRB-{62,64}/repeat-{1,2}/data/mcp-invocations/` and `results/artifacts/*/child-trajectories.json`. These paths are not publicly accessible; the aggregate evidence above is included to make the issue independently understandable.

Priority: non-fatal Harness efficiency/reliability follow-up. TC-E2E Judge stability is being fixed separately.
208.title: Track repeated arXiv 406/429 and queue timeouts across parallel research agents

## Problem

The local ScienceMemory backend can exhaust memory while building the folded session subgraph. A variable-length `next*0..` traversal enumerates paths across historical sessions before the requested session is filtered, and the interpreter materializes the intermediate rows before deduplication. A small stored graph can consequently require enormous query memory.

This remains reproducible on `feat/jiuwenswarm` at `7a1f0e37`. The relevant `query.py`, `_cypher.py`, and `local_backend.py` files have no diff from the historical incident checkout `d54cfc2d`.

## Historical incident and confidence boundary

During TC-E2E-01 on September 24, 2026:

- The startup log identifies PID 104627 as the memory-graph Python service, listening on port 17876.
- The contemporaneous incident record reports an OOM kill at 04:02:31 Asia/Shanghai, with anonymous RSS of 113,370,408 KiB (approximately 108.1 GiB) for that PID.
- The test stack was interrupted; TC-E2E-01 did not complete, and the next queued DRB-75 case was not started.

The original kernel entry is no longer available in the current journal/dmesg; the RSS figure comes from the retained incident record. There is no Python stack or heap profile from the instant of that OOM. The reproduction below establishes a current, concrete failure mechanism on retained data, but does not prove which exact request was executing at the historical OOM instant.

This is separate from the Node API trajectory/versioning memory problems observed with ScienceMemory disabled.

## Read-only reproduction on retained real graph data

The retained local store contains 4,520 nodes and 5,854 edges. The requested incident session has only **one node**.

Using current code, replay the JSONL records into a standalone in-memory `Graph`, then execute the SQL-like Cypher strings from `get_subgraph` with the incident session ID. Avoid constructing `Graph(Store(...))` directly against original evidence: loading may compact the store. Use a copy or read-only replay.

The diagnostic process was constrained to **512 MiB address space** and a **25-second alarm**. No model calls or service mutations were performed.

| Query | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Session nodes | 1 row, approximately 8 ms |
| Direct edges | 0 rows, approximately 18 ms |
| Folded surrogate-edge UNION | `MemoryError` after approximately 3.95 seconds, peak RSS approximately 502 MiB |
| Same folded query, with an early `WITH scope, first WHERE scope.session_id = $sid` before each variable-length match | 0 rows, approximately 1 ms |

The failure stack is inside `_match` / `_match_parts`. Early filtering is a diagnostic control, **not a complete fix**: querying an affected, branched session can still enumerate a huge number of paths.

## Mechanism

1. [`get_subgraph`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/query.py#L164) builds folded surrogate edges using:

   ```cypher
   MATCH (scope:Task)-[:contains]->(first:ToolCall)
   OPTIONAL MATCH (first)-[:next*0..]->(child:ToolCall)
   MATCH (child)-[:produces]->(c:Code)-[:produces]->(art:Artifact)
   WHERE scope.session_id = $sid
   ...
   RETURN DISTINCT ...
   ```

   The same traversal shape occurs in other UNION branches. The local interpreter does not push the later session predicate before the preceding variable-length match.

2. [`_walk`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/_cypher.py#L1290) tracks used relationships per path. It enumerates relationship-simple paths rather than unique reachable endpoints. A DAG can therefore cause combinatorial growth without any cycle.

3. [`_match`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/_cypher.py#L1171) appends all matching rows to a list. Projection, DISTINCT, and output LIMIT happen later, so small final output does not bound intermediate memory.

4. The retained `next` graph has 1,677 vertices and is acyclic, but contains **41 branching nodes**: 33 mix `scope_chain` and `temporal_chain` edges, four have multiple `scope_chain` edges, and four have multiple `temporal_chain` edges. This traversal does not filter by `method`. Dynamic programming on this DAG counts **237,316,988 paths, including zero-length paths, from one scope entry**.

5. [`LocalSession`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/7a1f0e37/services/memory-graph/src/sciencediscovery_memory_graph/local_backend.py#L48) uses a shared graph store across sessions and holds a graph-wide lock for the transaction. Historical data can affect a new nearly-empty session, and an expensive query can block other graph operations.

The origin of the extra chain branches is **not yet established**. Inspect chain rebuilding and scope/temporal edge membership rather than assuming a particular write race.

## Suggested fix scope

- Filter session/scope before traversal and prevent crossing unrelated scopes or chain types.
- For folded reachability views, compute the required reachable products/`via_child` identities without enumerating every path. Do not globally replace Cypher path semantics where callers actually require distinct paths.
- Investigate and validate chain construction/rebuild invariants; cover mixed chain types and historical stores.
- Add bounded intermediate-work/memory handling and cancellation so a graph query cannot take down the scientific task stack. Output limits alone are insufficient.
- Preserve low-volume query diagnostics: query identity, duration, graph size, traversal/intermediate counts, termination reason. Do not log sensitive graph contents by default.

## Acceptance / regression coverage

- A new nearly-empty session remains cheap to query when unrelated historical sessions contain branching chains.
- A deterministic small synthetic DAG with repeated branch/rejoin structure completes a folded reachability query with bounded work, correct deduplication, and preserved `via_child` information.
- Querying an affected session itself is safe; early session filtering alone is not considered sufficient.
- Cycles, mixed scope/temporal chains, rollback, and existing subgraph behavior retain their intended semantics.
- Validation runs under a strict process memory/time cap, avoiding another host OOM.

## Retained evidence

Local experiment-host paths (not publicly accessible):

- `/root/sciencediscovery-pr171-e2e-run/status.json` and `stack.log`
- `/root/.science-agent/memory-graph/{nodes,edges}.jsonl`
- `/root/sciencediscovery-memory-graph-diagnosis/{findings.md,probe.py,original-query.log,early-filter.log}`

The counts, query shape, guarded reproduction results, and uncertainty boundaries are included above so this issue is understandable without access to those private experiment files.
210.title: Memory graph local backend: folded subgraph path explosion can exhaust host memory

# 中文版

## 版本定位

ScienceDiscovery **全面拥抱 jiuwen-swarm 后端的第一个 Beta 版本**：保留科研工作台体验，以 jiuwen-swarm 支撑 Agent 执行，在新架构上整合科研专属能力。

本 issue 用于征集社区对 Release Note、发布范围及阻塞问题的反馈，**不是正式发布公告**。上一版本为 `0.2.0`；建议版本号为 **`0.3.0-beta.1`（待确认）**，开发主线为 `main`（原 JiuwenSwarm 分支已切换为主线），本次发版分支为 `releases/v0.3.0.beta`。

## Release Note 草案

### 重点支持场景

本版本重点保障以下四类场景，不追求一次性迁移全部历史能力或覆盖所有边界情况。

| 场景 | 主要流程与交付 | Domain 文档 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 文献调研 | 检索与获取文献、提取证据、多专家协作，交付带可追溯引用的调研报告 | [文献调研教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/literature-research.md) |
| 数据分析 | 读取数据、准备环境、执行分析，交付可复现代码、图表与结论 | [脓毒症数据分析教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/analyze-sepsis-endotypes.md) |
| 抗体设计 | 结合领域 Skill、专业模型和科研环境完成设计与筛选；依赖相应模型资源与算力，计算结果不等同于实验验证 | [抗体设计教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/antibody-design.md) |
| 算法优化 | 通过科研产物 RSI / Evolve 生成候选、执行评估与迭代，保留结果与过程记录 | [算法优化教程](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/zh/domains/evolve-a-solution.md) |

### 核心功能与改进

- **统一 JiuwenSwarm 默认后端**：源码、Docker 和发行包启动器均默认选择 JiuwenSwarm；保留显式 native 切换。主子 Agent 默认通过平台 `task` 委派、由 Swarm 执行，并非全面切换为 Swarm 原生多 Agent 编排。
- **科研执行环境与工作区**：支持本地/远程执行、托管环境、后台任务、文件传递、工作区交接及产物版本关联。
- **记忆图谱**：记录科研任务、文件与产物关系，支持引用追溯；源码及 Docker 部署提供默认本地存储，可选 Neo4j。
- **科研 Skill、MCP 与 Specialist**：支持内置能力和自定义扩展，组合专业专家完成科研任务。
- **科研产物 RSI 与 Idea Tree**：支持产物迭代优化、候选评估和研究思路的树状探索。
- **可观测性与测试**：完善执行轨迹、子任务状态和错误诊断，补充 Mock E2E、真实科研 Benchmark 与质量评估记录。
- **文档与入门体验**：整理中英文文档和四类场景教程，明确 Swarm/native 在上下文、规划、工具、Skill 等方面的行为差异。

这些功能包含已有能力的迁移与增强，并非全部首次引入。

### 官网、社区与交付配套（本版本新增）

- **统一对外网站**：提供[官网与安装入口](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html)，集中展示安装指引、使用文档与科研场景教程；网站内容随 `main` 分支同步更新。
- **用户交流社区**：面向海外与中国用户，分别建立 **Slack** 和 **飞书**用户交流群，用于使用交流、问题反馈与社区协作；加入方式见仓库首页。
- **双分支每日 CI**：构建每日质量检查，覆盖 `main` 和 `releases/v0.3.0.beta`。由 main 的定时任务触发两条分支各自的检查，分别保留结果、日志和构建产物，为主线演进与版本发布提供持续质量反馈。
- **多平台、多种安装方式**：支持 Linux、macOS，Windows 可通过 WSL 2 使用；提供源码、Linux 二进制发行包及 Docker 等部署方式。不同系统可用的安装方式与前置条件不同，详见[官网安装页](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html)。

### 主要 Bugfix

- **记忆图谱内存与查询性能**：修复折叠查询的路径爆炸，使用共享路径及累计集合预算，避免已复现的高内存分配；超预算返回结构化错误。优化会话索引查询，避免大量无关历史数据拖累新会话（#212，修复 #210）。
- **启动行为一致性**：修复源码与 Docker/发行包默认后端不一致，确保命令行后端选项优先于 `.env`；Docker 转发 Swarm 配置，E2E 显式选择后端（#214）。
- **Swarm/MCP 隔离与恢复**：改进模型、会话、工具绑定隔离，工具刷新、共享连接和权限生命周期（#173、#181、#182）。
- **子任务与远程执行可靠性**：改进并发排队、超时、取消、工作区交接和子 Agent 恢复；远程执行状态查询增加瞬时错误重试（#182、#187、#191）。
- **模型输出与事件流**：改进截断输出恢复，避免执行不完整工具参数，增强工具事件流存活与诊断（#190、#194）。
- **科研数据与交付**：改进 PDF 校验、arXiv 接入兼容性、产物版本关联，以及界面状态、快照作用域和取消诊断（#171、#180、#192、#179、#189、#193）。

## Beta 边界与升级说明

- **Nightly Real E2E 尚不稳定**：自动真实模型 E2E CI 仍在稳定化过程中，当前真实科研场景的验收以本地实际执行并保留记录的结果为准，需注明被测提交、模型和配置。Nightly 结果作为辅助诊断，不单独作为版本质量已达标的依据；跳过或隔离的用例不视为通过。UT/ST/Mock E2E 门禁仍是独立的质量依据。
- **部分安装路径为实验特性**：macOS Docker 以及所有 Windows 安装路径（包括 WSL 2 和 Docker Desktop）尚未全面验证 Agent 执行效果。当前预编译单文件包面向 Linux，不提供原生 macOS/Windows 二进制；macOS 优先使用源码方式，Windows 的 Linux 二进制/源码方式需在 WSL 2 内运行。具体支持范围与依赖见官网安装页。
- **官网与发行版的差异**：官网跟随 main，可能包含尚未进入本次 Beta 的更新；本版本的准确行为与限制以发行分支文档和最终 Release Note 为准。
- **场景验收与效果边界**：四类场景是重点验收范围，效果仍受模型、网络、数据源和算力影响；测试已加入不代表所有真实场景已稳定通过，发布以最终候选版本验收为准。
- **Swarm 初始化与后端切换**：源码首次使用 Swarm 前执行 `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`。保留原生循环可使用 `--no-jiuwenswarm` 或 `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native`。
- **记忆图谱升级与故障处理**：升级不会覆盖已保存的记忆功能设置；此前手动关闭的用户需在系统设置中重新开启。已有图谱可通过 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` 指向原目录，不自动迁移。设置 `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0` 可跳过服务；该可选服务启动失败时会报告原因并在禁用图谱的情况下继续启动，修正后需重启。
- **外部数据源限制**：arXiv 406/429、排队超时等外部数据源问题仍由 #208 跟踪。

## 社区反馈

请反馈：版本定位与版本号是否合适、功能或修复有无遗漏、四类场景是否存在发布阻塞，以及哪些限制必须写入正式说明。问题反馈请附配置、复现步骤及日志。

# English version

## Release positioning

This is ScienceDiscovery’s **first Beta release embracing the jiuwen-swarm backend**. It retains the scientific workbench experience, uses jiuwen-swarm for Agent execution, and integrates science-specific capabilities into the new architecture.

This issue collects community feedback on the release notes, scope, and blockers; **it is not a release announcement**. The previous version is `0.2.0`. The proposed version is **`0.3.0-beta.1` (to be confirmed)**, with development on `main` (the former JiuwenSwarm branch) and this release prepared from `releases/v0.3.0.beta`.

## Draft release notes

### Priority scenarios

This Beta focuses on four scientific workflows rather than migrating every historical capability or covering every corner case.

| Scenario | Workflow and deliverables | Domain documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literature review | Search and retrieve literature, extract evidence, collaborate across specialists, and deliver a report with traceable citations | [Literature research tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/literature-research.md) |
| Data analysis | Inspect data, prepare an environment, execute analysis, and deliver reproducible code, figures, and conclusions | [Sepsis data analysis tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/analyze-sepsis-endotypes.md) |
| Antibody design | Combine domain Skills, specialized models, and scientific environments for design and screening; requires appropriate model resources and compute, and computational results do not constitute experimental validation | [Antibody design tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/antibody-design.md) |
| Algorithm optimization | Generate, evaluate, and iterate on candidates through scientific-artifact RSI / Evolve, retaining results and execution records | [Evolve a solution tutorial](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/releases/v0.3.0.beta/docs/en/domains/evolve-a-solution.md) |

### Core capabilities and improvements

- **Consistent JiuwenSwarm default**: source, Docker, and packaged launchers now select JiuwenSwarm by default, with an explicit native opt-out. Subagents default to platform `task` delegation with Swarm execution—not a complete switch to Swarm-native multi-agent orchestration.
- **Scientific environments and workspaces**: local/remote execution, managed environments, background tasks, file transfers, workspace handoffs, and artifact-version associations.
- **Memory graph**: research-task, file, and artifact relationships with traceable citations; source and Docker deployments provide local storage by default, with optional Neo4j.
- **Scientific Skills, MCP, and Specialists**: built-in capabilities and custom extensions for domain-expert collaboration.
- **Scientific-artifact RSI and Idea Tree**: iterative artifact optimization, candidate evaluation, and tree-based exploration of research ideas.
- **Observability and testing**: improved trajectories, subtask status, and diagnostics, alongside Mock E2E, real scientific benchmarks, and quality-evaluation records.
- **Documentation and onboarding**: reorganized English/Chinese documentation and tutorials for the four workflows, with explicit Swarm/native differences in context, planning, tools, and Skills.

These include migrations and enhancements of existing capabilities, not exclusively new features.

### Website, community, and delivery infrastructure (new in this release)

- **Unified public website**: the [website and installation hub](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html) bring together installation guidance, documentation, and scientific workflow tutorials. Website content is kept in sync with `main`.
- **User communities**: **Slack** and **Feishu** groups have been established for international and China-based users respectively, supporting usage discussions, feedback, and community collaboration. See the repository homepage for joining instructions.
- **Daily CI for both branches**: daily quality checks cover `main` and `releases/v0.3.0.beta`. The scheduled main workflow triggers independent runs for both branches, retaining separate results, logs, and build artifacts to support development and release validation.
- **Multiple platforms and installation options**: Linux and macOS are supported, with Windows access through WSL 2. Options include source installation, Linux binary packages, and Docker. Availability and prerequisites vary by platform; see the [installation hub](https://sciencediscovery.github.io/install/index.html).

### Major fixes

- **Memory-graph query performance and memory use**: eliminate path explosion in folded queries, introduce shared paths and cumulative collection budgets for reproduced allocation failures, and return structured budget errors. Indexed session queries avoid scanning unrelated historical data (#212, fixes #210).
- **Consistent startup behavior**: align source defaults with Docker/packages, make CLI backend selection override `.env`, forward Swarm settings through Docker, and select E2E backends explicitly (#214).
- **Swarm/MCP isolation and recovery**: improve model/session/tool binding isolation, tool refresh, shared connections, and permission lifecycle (#173, #181, #182).
- **Subtask and remote-execution reliability**: improve admission queues, timeouts, cancellation, workspace handoffs, and subagent resumption; retry transient remote execution-status failures (#182, #187, #191).
- **Model output and event streams**: recover from output truncation without executing incomplete tool arguments, and improve tool-stream liveness and diagnostics (#190, #194).
- **Scientific data and delivery**: improve PDF validation, arXiv compatibility, artifact-version associations, UI state, snapshot scope, and cancellation diagnostics (#171, #180, #192, #179, #189, #193).

## Beta limitations and upgrade notes

- **Nightly Real E2E is not yet stable**: automated real-model E2E CI is still being stabilized. For now, acceptance of real scientific workflows relies on recorded local runs, identifying the tested commit, model, and configuration. Nightly results provide supplementary diagnostics, not standalone proof of release readiness. Skipped or quarantined cases are not passes; UT/ST/Mock E2E gates remain independent quality evidence.
- **Some installation paths are experimental**: macOS Docker and all Windows paths (including WSL 2 and Docker Desktop) have not been fully validated for Agent execution. Current prepackaged single-file binaries target Linux, not native macOS or Windows. Prefer source installation on macOS; Linux binaries/source installation on Windows run inside WSL 2. Consult the installation hub for platform-specific requirements and support boundaries.
- **Website versus release documentation**: the website follows main and may describe updates not yet included in this Beta. Use the release-branch documentation and final release notes for the exact behavior and limitations of this version.
- **Workflow acceptance and outcome limitations**: The four workflows are priority acceptance targets. Outcomes depend on the model, network, data sources, and compute. Having tests does not establish that all real scenarios pass reliably; release acceptance must use the final candidate.
- **Swarm setup and backend selection**: Before first using Swarm from source, run `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup`. Use `--no-jiuwenswarm` or `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXECUTOR=native` to retain the native loop.
- **Memory-graph upgrades and failure handling**: Upgrades preserve saved memory preferences; users who previously disabled memory must re-enable it in System Settings. Use `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_DATA_DIR` to retain an existing graph directory; data is not migrated automatically. Set `SCIENCE_AGENT_MEMORY_GRAPH_AVAILABLE=0` to skip the service. If this optional service fails to start, the launcher reports the cause and continues with memory disabled; correct the cause and restart.
- **External data-source limitations**: External-source failures, including arXiv 406/429 responses and queue timeouts, remain tracked in #208.

## Community feedback

Please comment on release positioning/versioning, missing features or fixes, blockers in the four workflows, and limitations that must appear in the final notes. Include configuration, reproduction steps, and logs for reported problems.

## Problem

Successful real research runs still have a large per-case memory footprint for individual users. On current `feat/jiuwenswarm`, the highest observed worker cgroup peak is **11.12 GiB**. Although the latest GraphMemory fix prevented the previously observed runaway behavior in this experiment, this steady operational footprint deserves separate investigation and reduction for ordinary personal computers.

This is a resource-efficiency issue, not a report of another GraphMemory OOM. It is separate from #210 / its fix #212.

## Measured evidence

Experiment revision: `17d0774a` (includes #212 and TC Judge fix #209).

- Nine real scientific E2E cases, three repetitions each; four case workers concurrently.
- GraphMemory enabled throughout, local backend, isolated graph directory per case/repetition.
- Native task dispatch with Swarm execution; generator/Judge `deepseek-flash`.
- Each worker has a 24 GiB cgroup limit and no swap. The group includes the platform stack, graph service, Swarm, Runner and descendants, browser, and Judge.
- All 27 attempts delivered successfully. Retained `memory.events` show `max=0`, `oom=0`, `oom_kill=0` for every worker.

| Case / repetition | Worker cgroup peak (GiB) | Sampled Node API RSS peak (GiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| TC-E2E-01 / 1 | 11.124 | 0.977 |
| DRB-75 / 1 | 11.123 | 1.127 |
| DRB-62 / 2 | 10.796 | 0.952 |
| DRB-75 / 3 | 10.397 | 1.275 |
| DRB-59 / 2 | 10.107 | 1.080 |

The three worker peaks for TC-E2E-01 were 11.12 / 8.27 / 8.43 GiB; DRB-75 was 11.12 / 8.61 / 10.40 GiB. Even PUCT's workers peaked around 4.41 GiB in this setup.

**Measurement boundaries:**

- Cgroup peak includes charged file cache and other memory, not just anonymous RSS. It is not proof that the application requires 11 GiB of unreclaimable working memory.
- API RSS is sampled separately and its maximum need not coincide with the group peak. Do not subtract these maxima to infer another component's usage.
- GraphMemory did not appear in the retained high-RSS process samples, but these contain only the host's top 12 processes above a threshold, so its precise individual peak cannot be recovered.
- This harness includes Playwright and diagnostic sampling. Startup/provisioning, browser, diagnostics, page cache, child agents, and runtime costs must be separated before attributing the footprint to the product or GraphMemory.
- Concurrent cases and agent choices varied; this is not a controlled concurrency-scaling measurement.

## Why this matters

Users on 8–16 GiB machines also need memory for the OS, browser, and other applications. Raising per-worker limits or recommending large-memory hosts is not an adequate resource-efficiency strategy. We need to establish the actual working set and provide a practical personal-machine configuration without silently dropping research evidence or quality requirements.

## Investigation and optimization plan

1. Record `memory.stat` (`anon`, `file`, `kernel`, `slab`, etc.), `memory.current/peak/events`, and memory pressure alongside process-tree attribution for the **specific worker cgroup**. Capture phase markers for startup, provisioning, child research, synthesis, and grading.
2. Sample process RSS/PSS by role: API, Swarm/gateway, graph, Runner/executions, browser, Judge. Keep diagnostics lightweight and credential-free; measure profiler overhead explicitly.
3. Reproduce TC-E2E-01 and DRB-75 alone and with concurrent child tasks. Measure the idle stack separately and compare with/without the browser/profiling overhead. Preserve GraphMemory and the same delivery/scoring contract.
4. Identify avoidable duplication or retention only from profiles: repeated runtime processes, scientific environments/imports, per-agent contexts, trajectory buffers, graph state, caches, and teardown. Do not assume any one is the culprit from aggregate peaks.
5. Optimize the dominant confirmed contributors. If required, provide explicit resource-aware concurrency/backpressure and document the latency tradeoff rather than changing research tasks or silently disabling capabilities.

## Acceptance criteria

- Produce a component/phase memory breakdown for the highest-footprint cases, distinguishing reclaimable cache from working memory.
- Establish a measured baseline and a concrete lower memory budget suitable for a representative personal machine, with headroom for OS and interactive use; do not invent a target before attribution.
- Demonstrate improvement against that baseline on the same tasks, with GraphMemory enabled, no OOM, retained artifact delivery, and quality scoring reported independently.
- Check memory release after task completion and repeated use within a long-lived session; include lightweight regression monitoring where practical.

Retained evidence on the experiment host (not publicly accessible):
`/root/sciencediscovery-real9-graph-3x-20260927/case-summary.csv`, plus each case's `memory.csv`, `memory-events.txt`, and `memory-profiles/memory-*.jsonl`.

## Summary

Long agent runs spend an increasing amount of time synchronously publishing trajectory records before the next model request. The main source is repeated full transitive-closure validation in the ScienceDiscovery CAS ref publication path.

This is visible with the JiuwenSwarm executor because it records every model request and completed turn through `AgentVersionRecorder`, but the expensive closure walk is implemented by ScienceDiscovery, not JiuwenSwarm.

The behavior was reproduced at commit `5de0ff59eb0375f45d93a065ec701ca6573fc328`.

## Scope

This does not appear to be enabled only by CI:

- `createAgentRun()` supplies `versioning` for every normal agent run.
- `JiuwenSwarmTrajectory` creates an `AgentVersionRecorder` whenever `versioning` is present.
- `SCIENCE_AGENT_TRACE_GATEWAY_PROGRESS=1` only adds progress logging around the same operations. It does not enable trajectory persistence, and the Nightly workflow does not set it.

Therefore ordinary local/UI runs use the same trajectory recording path. Short runs usually hide the cost; long histories amplify it.

## Evidence from two BiomniBench runs

Both runs disabled subagents, so child-agent execution is not required to reproduce the slowdown.

| Case | Session span | Completed model outputs | Model request time | Tool time | Time outside measured model/tool intervals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 76m 32.7s | 74 | 27m 39.7s | 7m 31.3s | 42m 59.3s |
| DA-14-1 | 81m 36.8s | 73 | 30m 47.8s | 10m 24.6s | 41m 55.6s |

The interval around a turn was split at `state.committed`:

| Case | Last tool to state committed | State committed to next model input | Combined |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 17m 57.0s | 19m 50.7s | 37m 47.7s |
| DA-14-1 | 15m 43.8s | 20m 56.4s | 36m 40.2s |

Per-turn combined medians grew with turn count:

| Case | Turns 0-19 | Turns 20-49 | Turns 50+ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | 9.2s | 22.9s | 55.2s |
| DA-14-1 | 6.8s | 25.5s | 59.3s |

This time is shown under the broad UI `thinking` phase, but much of it occurs before the next model request has been sent.

## Direct CAS measurements

On the preserved DA-13-3 CAS:

- Step 5: 100 reachable objects, 4.1 MiB, 449-518ms to validate.
- Step 20: 346 objects, 22.9 MiB, about 1.7-2.1s.
- Step 50: 755 objects, 81.7 MiB, about 4.4-6.0s.
- Step 73: 989 objects, 141.6 MiB, about 7-11s.
- The model-input context closure at turn 74 contained 992 objects and took 9.27s to validate.

At least two such commits are on each turn's critical path: the exact model-input/context ref and the completed trajectory step.

A separate 70-turn synthetic `AgentVersionRecorder` benchmark used no model, network, web search, Jina, or subagent calls. It still showed:

- `after_assembly` median: 193ms for turns 0-19, 1,488ms for turns 50-69.
- `after_turn` median: 275ms for turns 0-19, 1,601ms for turns 50-69.
- Total runtime was about two minutes.

## Root cause

`RefStore.commit()` calls `VersionStore.validateClosure(target)` before every ref transaction. `validateClosure()` reads and hashes every reachable object. Trajectory steps strongly reference prior steps, snapshots, contexts, actions, and event segments, so the reachable closure grows with every turn.

Revalidating all immutable ancestors on every publication makes a long trajectory approximately quadratic in total validation work.

Relevant paths:

- `packages/cas/src/versioning.ts`: `VersionStore.validateClosure()` and `RefStore.commit()`.
- `services/api/src/native-agent/versioning.ts`: context and step ref commits.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-trajectory.ts`: synchronous recording around model requests and completed turns.

## Isolated prototype

An offline prototype kept the public `validateClosure()` as a full byte/hash audit. For commit-time validation it:

1. Still traverses every reachable object.
2. Caches each successfully verified object's dependencies and filesystem identity (`dev`, `ino`, `size`, `mtimeNs`, `ctimeNs`).
3. Skips rereading and rehashing an object only when that identity is unchanged.
4. Falls back to full verification if the object is new or its metadata changed.
5. Publishes cache entries only after the entire closure succeeds.

Results:

| Measurement | Current implementation | Prototype |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 70-turn late `after_assembly` median | 1,488ms | 168ms |
| 70-turn late `after_turn` median | 1,601ms | 252ms |
| 70-turn total runtime | about 120s | 29.7s |
| Real DA-13-3 steps 50-73 validation | final scans about 7-11s each | 409ms median, 535ms max |
| Replay all 74 DA-13-3 history roots | not measured as one batch | 20.7s total |

The two late-turn critical recording stages fell from about 3.09s to 0.42s, an 86% reduction in the synthetic run.

The prototype passed all 26 CAS tests. Tests also confirmed that a previously verified dependency is still rejected after deletion and after same-size content corruption.

## Expected behavior

Trajectory recording should remain available for exports, provenance, recovery, and debugging, but its synchronous per-turn cost should depend mainly on newly published objects rather than the size of the full historical trajectory.

## Possible direction

- Add an incremental commit-validation path while retaining an explicit full audit API.
- Consider a persistent verified-object index or storage generation if reuse across API restarts is needed.
- Keep full hash audits available on read/export, startup, background verification, or an explicit integrity operation.
- Add stage duration metrics for workspace snapshot, context publication, step publication, history serialization, SQLite commit, and model request so future stalls are attributable without multi-gigabyte artifact analysis.

The metadata-cache prototype has a trust boundary: a privileged actor able to rewrite bytes while preserving inode, size, mtime, and ctime could evade the commit fast path. A production design should document that assumption or use a stronger persistent verification mechanism.

This optimization does not address model latency, web/tool latency, workspace snapshot cost, history serialization, or the separate 240s no-progress failure observed after a final captured context.
230.title: Trajectory CAS commit validation grows quadratically in long agent runs

## What happened

Nightly real-model E2E fails the whole Daily gate when a single request to the configured OpenAI-compatible model gateway returns a provider error. Other cases in the same job still pass, and the same case can pass on another run the same night.

On 2026-10-06, main Nightly run [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`) executed 10 real cases: 5 passed, 5 failed, 0 skipped, in 3.0 hours. The job uses `E2E_LLM_MODEL=deepseek-v4-flash` and `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL=https://yibuapi.com/v1`. Playwright is configured with `retries: 0` and one worker.

Three of those failures were gateway responses, and the product already showed them:

- **DRB-75** failed in 9.3 seconds. No subagent and no tool call ran. The page showed error 181001: HTTP 500 from the gateway, body `Database error, please contact the administrator`, type `new_api_error`.
- **PUCT-COMPRESS** failed in 11.5 seconds with the same HTTP 500 text in `run.error`. No search started.
- **workspace plan and run-anchored subagent** failed after 7.0 minutes. The page already showed HTTP 503: `No available channel for model deepseek-v4-flash under group default (distributor)`, code `model_not_found`, wrapped as the same 181001 gateway error. The test then waited out a 420 second timeout for a plan section that never appeared.

The other five cases in that job passed, including DRB-58 after 51.0 minutes and TC-E2E-01 after 43.0 minutes. The same three cases passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`releases/v0.3.0.beta` at `6d3c49a8`) the same night. The previous night, that same beta commit passed all 10 real cases in [37382672011](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37382672011).

## Why this is a product/CI problem

The gateway is failing one request at a time, not the whole job. A 500 or 503 still fails the real-E2E job, which fails Nightly. There is no retry, and the suite does not record these as an external provider fault separate from a product regression.

## Expected

A transient gateway 500 or 503 is visible as that provider error. One such request does not have the same meaning as a product run that finished and failed to deliver. Cases that passed in the same job stay visible as passes.

## Evidence limits

This does not say the gateway was down for the whole job. It also does not cover the research cases that ran for about 20 minutes and then ended without a report; those are separate failures.
232.title: bug(ci): Nightly real E2E fails the gate on one transient model-gateway 500 or 503

233.author: zhaozhaozz
233.body:
## What happened

Several real-E2E failures show up in GitHub Actions as only this assertion:

```text
Error: Main run must complete and reference a readable nonempty final artifact
Expected: "passed"
Received: "failed"
```

`delivery.status` comes from `deliveryStatus(runStatus, delivered)` in `test/helpers/real-delivery.mjs`. An empty delivered-artifact list returns `"failed"`. That string does not say whether the run status was `failed`, `running`, or `completed`, and it does not include `run.error`.

The assertion is at `test/deepresearchbench-swarm.spec.ts` (the `expect(delivery.status, "Main run must complete and reference a readable nonempty final artifact")` check) and the same check in `test/science-research-team-real.spec.ts`. The DeepResearch spec stores the assertion text into `metrics.error` in the `catch` block, so the attached benchmark metrics also lose the product error.

On main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), DRB-59, DRB-62, and DRB-75 all printed that assertion. The failure-page text was different for each:

- DRB-75: gateway HTTP 500, `Database error, please contact the administrator`.
- DRB-59: `Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell)`.
- DRB-62: `interaction round execution failed`.

`test/evolve-compression-real.spec.ts` already throws ``Main run ${run.status}: ${run.error}``, so PUCT-COMPRESS printed the HTTP 500 in the Actions log. The DeepResearch and team specs do not.

## Expected

When `delivery.status` is not `"passed"`, the Actions log includes the run status and the product error string that the page already shows. An empty artifact list and a gateway 500 remain distinguishable without opening the trace.

## Evidence limits

`collectFinalDelivery` returns `run_status`, `answer`, `artifacts`, and content-read errors. For these failures `delivery.errors` was empty because no artifact was selected. The product error was on the page, not in that array.

234.body:
## What happened

The real journey `workspace plan and run-anchored subagent survive follow-up and reload` in `test/issue-67-34-inline-cards.spec.ts` waits up to 420 seconds for `aside.workspace-panel [data-folder="tasks"] details.workspace-plan-section` to become visible (`showWorkspacePlans`).

```text
[181001] model call failed ... Error code: 503 ...
No available channel for model deepseek-v4-flash under group default (distributor)
type new_api_error
```

235.author: zhaozhaozz
235.body:
## What happened

A long real research run can end with only this text on the page:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · interaction round execution failed
```

The sentence before the dot is `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`. The detail after the dot is the fixed string `interaction round execution failed`. In the DeepAgent interaction-round handler that string replaces the caught exception: the handler logs the exception and returns `error_code=round_execution_error` with that fixed message. The original exception does not reach the page or the E2E log.

Observed runs, both with an empty final answer and `delivery.status` `"failed"`:

- main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-62**, 23.7 minutes. One subagent completed. The session had `literature_sources.json` and showed 271K usage and 20 executions. The required `deepresearchbench-62.md` was not delivered. Run status was `failed`.
- release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) (`6d3c49a8`), **DRB-58**, 21.0 minutes. Run status was `failed`. The session had `literature_sources.json`, `hgt_animals_sources.md`, and `hgt_plants_sources.md`. One child was `completed` and another was still `running`. A PubMed call had returned HTTP 429 from `eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov`. Literature-connector 429s are already tracked in #208.

The same DRB-62 passed on the beta run (36.1 minutes), and the same DRB-58 passed on the main run (51.0 minutes). The model and gateway had already served those sessions for about 20 minutes, so this is not a wrong API key or a missing model id.

## Expected

The failed round keeps the underlying exception message (gateway status, tool error, or runtime exception) in the run error that the page and the test can read. A round that ran for many minutes is not described only as a model-configuration rejection.

## Evidence limits

The server log for these two runs was not retrieved, so the exception that was swallowed is not known. The page text and the run status are known.

236.body:
## What happened

A real research run that has already been working can stop because the model gateway rejects one tool call whose arguments do not parse. The same happens to a subagent that has already finished its work. The page then tells the user to check the model configuration.

On main Nightly [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`), **DRB-59** ran for 20.2 minutes. Both subagents completed. The session contained `navigation_cues_summary.md`, `navigation_cues_sources.json`, `disturbance_summary.md`, and `disturbance_sources.json`, and the page showed 167K usage. The required `deepresearchbench-59.md` was not among them. The final answer was empty and the run status was `failed`.

The request error on the failure page was:

```text
The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry. · Model returned invalid tool arguments (tools: run_shell); gateway request chatcmpl-a2101146-60b8-4549-a033-1fe6f70bcfa0
```

The same DRB-59 passed on the release-branch Nightly [37529816020](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529816020) in 1.3 hours. The gateway and model id had already completed two subagents in the failing run.

On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) (`90db5b8e`), the same failure ended two more journeys, once on an MCP tool rather than `run_shell`. All three events below are logged as `"truncated":false` in the server log's `[model-arguments]` line. The server log has no 5xx or 429 on model calls during the journeys.

| Journey | Where it failed | Gateway request | Tool | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DRB-64 | Main run, after 23 minutes. Both subagents had completed, and the main agent had just said it would write the report. | `chatcmpl-2c3cbc55-d420-4a0e-ab0f-f460883c3061` | `run_shell` | Run `failed`, empty final answer. The session had three files from the subagents (two source packages and coverage notes); the required `deepresearchbench-64.md` was never declared. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 1st attempt. Its `deliverable_check` MCP call had already returned `ok: true`; it failed while writing `signoff.json`. | `chatcmpl-34b150cd-8aa4-478d-8c60-f6b6de204c62` | `run_shell` | Subagent `failed`. |
| TC-E2E-01 | Delivery-signoff subagent, 2nd attempt, on its `deliverable_check` call, which was to carry the full 26,226-byte report. | `chatcmpl-f980e9ac-a76a-422a-af31-11a515383f8f` | MCP `deliverable_check` | Subagent `failed`. The checker never received the call. |

In TC-E2E-01 all five research specialists had completed within 37 minutes and `evidence_brief.md` (26,226 bytes) existed. The two signoff failures and their re-dispatches used the remaining time; the third signoff attempt was still running when the 55-minute test budget ran out, and the test cancelled the run, which had no final answer. How the test reports a run cut off by its budget is #239.

## Why one call ends the run

Code at `90db5b8e`; these files are unchanged on main at `9189206d`.

1. `packages/model/src/client.ts` parses each assembled tool call with `JSON.parse` ([L221-L230](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L221-L230)) and sets `argsParseError` on failure.
2. In the JiuwenSwarm model gateway, `rejectInvalidArguments` ([L220-L228](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L220-L228)) lets truncated turns through to the output-limit recovery, but throws for any non-truncated call with `argsParseError`. The gateway answers that turn with an error (an SSE error event once streaming has started, otherwise HTTP 502). Swarm does not retry the turn, and `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` ([L363-L367](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L363-L367)) turns it into the error of the run or subagent.
3. `classifyRunFailure` ([services/api/src/run-failure.ts L28-L49](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/run-failure.ts#L28-L49)) matches none of its markers for this message and falls through to `semantic-error`. The Web UI renders that class as `runFailure.semantic-error` in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts`: "The model service rejected the request. Check the model configuration and input, then retry."

The same condition is handled three different ways:

- Native runtime: `packages/tools/src/registry.ts` ([L334-L338](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/tools/src/registry.ts#L334-L338)) returns `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS` with `retryable: true` to the model as a tool result, and the model can re-issue the call.
- Swarm, truncated call: the calls are withheld and the turn goes through bounded output-limit recovery. In Nightly 37875334064 two such events (03:57 and 04:42 UTC) did not end their runs, and those journeys (DRB-58, DRB-62) passed.
- Swarm, non-truncated call: the run or subagent fails.

Passing the call through unchanged would be worse: the gateway re-serializes calls from their parsed arguments (`toolCallsOf`, [L123-L125](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L123-L125)), so Swarm would execute the tool with `{}`.

## Where it fails: in ScienceDiscovery, before JiuwenSwarm sees the call

Every model request from JiuwenSwarm passes two ScienceDiscovery layers before it reaches the provider:

```text
JiuwenSwarm -> adapter /llm/<token>/v1/chat/completions (services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py)
            -> Node model gateway (services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts)
            -> packages/model client -> provider
```

`jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` points Swarm's model at `modelGateway.url` ([L555](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts#L555)), and the adapter route forwards to that URL. The gateway drops the whole turn before Swarm receives the tool call. Swarm only gets an error for its model request; it does not retry that request, and its agent loop ends.

JiuwenSwarm's own handling would not end the run. JiuwenSwarm `workswarm0.2.6` pins agent-core (`openjiuwen`) at `ad0c9dfb`, whose `openjiuwen/core/single_agent/ability_manager.py` parses tool arguments in `_parse_tool_arguments_with_repair`: `json.loads`, then a bracket-balancing repair, and if both fail `execute` raises `AbilityExecutionError` whose `ToolMessage` (`Invalid tool arguments JSON: …`) is returned to the model as the tool result, "so it can self-correct". The native ScienceDiscovery runtime does the same with `INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS`.

A second ScienceDiscovery layer would reject the same call for platform tools. The adapter's `StreamingToolRewriter` parses the complete arguments of each platform tool with `json.loads` at `finish_reason` to append the run tag ([L328](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L328)), and on failure ends the stream with `invalid streamed platform tool arguments` ([L362-L366](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L362-L366)). It was not reached in these runs because the gateway had already stopped the turn. Simply passing the call through to Swarm would hit this layer, and would also put unparseable arguments into the history replayed to the provider.

## Expected

- A non-truncated call whose arguments do not parse is not executed, and the model is told which call failed and why so that it can re-issue it, with a bounded number of attempts (the same shape as the truncated-call recovery, or a bounded re-sample in the gateway). One bad call does not end a run that has been working for 20 to 40 minutes, and does not fail a subagent that has already finished its work.
- This holds for every tool, including MCP tools, in the main run and in subagents.
- If recovery is exhausted, the run error says that the model produced an invalid tool call, with the tool name and gateway request id. The user-facing text does not tell the user to check the model configuration when the same model has already been calling tools in that run.
- The Actions log for the journey includes this error instead of only `delivery.status` `"failed"` (#233).

## Evidence limits

Neither Nightly captured the raw argument strings or the parser messages, so whether the model emitted malformed JSON or the stream assembler lost part of the arguments is not known. Making that distinguishable is #246.

## What happened

During the same DRB-59 run, a subagent's `declare_artifact` call was rejected before the run later stopped on invalid `run_shell` arguments.

Nightly: main [37529799288](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37529799288) (`7a032425`). The tool error was:

```text
[182301] execute invoke failed, error='[189002] format data with schema failed, error='1 validation error for DynamicModel
artifacts
  Extra inputs are not permitted [type=extra_forbidden, input_value=[{'path': 'navigation_cues_sources.json', 'name': 'navigation_cues_sources.json', 'description': '...'}], input_type=list]

The schema rejects the extra field, and the tool result is that raw validation error.

A `declare_artifact` call that puts the file list under `artifacts` gets a tool result that names the accepted fields (`path` or `paths`) and can be retried. ## Evidence limits

Only this one call was captured. It does not show that every `declare_artifact` batch fails. The description already tells the model to use `path` or `paths`.

## What happened

The real team journey fails when the main run is still `running` at the team budget, because the final answer has not cited an artifact yet.

`test/science-research-team-real.spec.ts` polls until the run status is `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`, or until `E2E_TEAM_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` (Nightly sets this to `3300000`, 55 minutes; the spec default is 60 minutes). The previous night, the same beta commit passed this journey inside a fully green 10-case real job ([37382672011](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37382672011)).

A run that is still `running` when the budget expires is reported as still running, including how long it ran and that cancel was requested. It is not reported as the same `delivery.status` `"failed"` used when a run has finished with no cited artifact. 245.author: wyhohyw
245.body:
## Summary

Biomni real E2E shows large endpoint-dependent variation in model-request latency and total generation time. Earlier runs through an OpenAI-compatible relay also ended after a terminal model turn with no text or tool call. We need enough safe wire-level diagnostics to tell an upstream empty completion from an SSE/parser defect, and to separate model/API latency from agent work.

This is distinct from #232, which records explicit HTTP 500/503 gateway errors.

## Local measurements

The two Biomni cases were run in parallel on the same Windows/WSL machine, with evaluation disabled, the `task` tool removed (no subagents), and no Jina key. `generation` is the benchmark's generation duration; request timing is the elapsed time of completed `[model-stream]` requests in `stack.log`. All rows below passed delivery. The relay run used `https://yibuapi.com/v1` with model alias `deepseek-v4.1-flash`; the direct runs used `https://api.deepseek.com` with model alias `deepseek-flash`.

| Case | Endpoint / runs | Generation | Completed model requests | Median request | Reported total tokens |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DA-13-3 | relay, r5 | 37.46 min | 71 | 25.16 s | 504,634 |
| DA-13-3 | direct, r6/r7/r9/r10 | 5.71–20.67 min | 26–44 | 6.10–13.93 s | 118,066–140,022 |
| DA-14-1 | relay, r5 | 31.31 min | 63 | 20.18 s | 177,043 |
| DA-14-1 | direct, r6/r9/r10 | 20.75–35.79 min | 54–72 | 11.59–19.01 s | 191,883–284,635 |

The seven direct samples all passed delivery, with zero reported SSE parse errors or SSE error records. Earlier local relay samples had a normalized final model turn with empty text, no tool call, and `finish_reason=stop`, after which the run was marked completed without the expected deliverable. Those older samples did **not** retain raw SSE records, so they cannot establish whether the upstream service sent an empty completion or the local stream adapter lost content. The direct samples also used a local empty-turn guard and SSE parsing fixes, so the passing rate is **not** an isolated endpoint A/B result.

## Why the current evidence is insufficient

- The relay and direct runs used different model aliases. The model's chosen steps, request counts, and token totals varied substantially, so total-duration differences are not an estimate of API latency alone.
- Even with the same direct endpoint, DA-13-3 varied from 5.71 to 20.67 minutes, and DA-14-1 from 20.75 to 35.79 minutes. Agent behavior and task content remain major contributors.
- A normalized empty final turn does not reveal whether the wire response was empty, malformed, or incorrectly mapped locally.

## Requested investigation / acceptance criteria

1. Save privacy-safe per-request diagnostics in real E2E artifacts: endpoint identity and model alias, request ID, HTTP status, dispatch/headers/first byte/first SSE record/completion timestamps, SSE record and parse-error counts, final content/tool-call presence, `finish_reason`, and retry/error classification. Do not save credentials or prompt/response bodies in the default diagnostic log.
2. Treat an empty terminal assistant turn with no tool call as an error rather than a successful final answer. Preserve the upstream request ID and framing summary when this occurs.
3. Compare relay and direct endpoints with the same model, request body, workload, and concurrency. Report per-request latency distributions separately from total agent duration and token use.
4. In CI summaries, identify explicit provider failures, empty completions, and local parse/mapping failures separately from research-quality failures.

I can provide the local benchmark metrics and sanitized `[model-stream]`/`[model-sse-summary]` excerpts if useful. No API keys or prompt contents are included here.

246.author: zhaozhaozz
246.body:
## What happened

On main Nightly [37875334064](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/37875334064) (`90db5b8e`), three tool calls from `deepseek-v4-flash` had arguments that `JSON.parse` rejected. None of them was truncated. #236 describes what each one did to its run. The upstream answered each of these requests with a complete response (the gateway logged its token usage), none of the three ended with `finish_reason: "length"`, and the server log has no 5xx or 429 on model calls during the journeys.

| Journey | Agent | Gateway request | Tool-call id | Tool |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DRB-64 | main run | `chatcmpl-2c3cbc55-d420-4a0e-ab0f-f460883c3061` | `call_f86a6970436f4559a83bd896` | `run_shell` |
| TC-E2E-01 | delivery-signoff subagent, 1st attempt | `chatcmpl-34b150cd-8aa4-478d-8c60-f6b6de204c62` | `call_00_7q1ei5oo6oy4v6d6mobdo6rw` | `run_shell` |
| TC-E2E-01 | delivery-signoff subagent, 2nd attempt | `chatcmpl-f980e9ac-a76a-422a-af31-11a515383f8f` | `call_00_f9fauxgae0v8n954s1db7ijo` | MCP `deliverable_check` |

From this evidence nobody can tell whether the model produced invalid JSON or our client lost part of the streamed arguments. The `[model-arguments]` line in the server log carries only the request id, tool name, tool-call id, usage and the truncation flag. The opt-in file `SCIENCE_AGENT_INVALID_TOOL_ARGUMENTS_FILE` keeps the parser message and the assembled arguments (see "Invalid tool argument diagnostics" in `jiuwen_swarm/README.md`), but Nightly real E2E does not set it.

The pattern fits both explanations:

- Each failing call carried a long text in a string argument: the DRB-64 main agent had just said it would write the report, the first signoff attempt was writing `signoff.json`, and the second was passing the full 26,226-byte report as `report_text`. Long strings are where a model is most likely to mis-escape JSON. They are also where a stream has the most fragments.
- In the same TC-E2E-01 run, the first signoff attempt had passed the same 26,226-byte `report_text` to `deliverable_check` successfully about five minutes before the second attempt failed on it.
- The tool-call ids come in two formats (`call_<24 hex>` and `call_00_<id>`), so at least two upstream channels behind the same endpoint showed the symptom. That does not separate the explanations either: the client is the same for both.

## Stream-assembly paths that would leave no trace

In [`packages/model/src/client.ts`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts) at `90db5b8e` (the file is unchanged on main at `9189206d`):

- [L536-L540](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L536-L540): a `data:` payload that fails `JSON.parse` is skipped with `continue`. Nothing counts or logs it. If the skipped chunk was in the middle of a tool call, the call keeps its name, the response still ends normally, and the arguments have a gap.
- [L232-L249](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L232-L249) (`sseData`): every `data:` line is yielded as a complete payload. An event whose data spans several `data:` lines would be split, and the rule above would then skip the parts. A last line without a trailing newline is never yielded.
- [L587](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/90db5b8e085c8afeceee8ad66a0eec2cece718ed/packages/model/src/client.ts#L587): a tool-call delta without `index` is stored under `fragments.size`, i.e. as a new call. A continuation fragment without `index` would be separated from its call, and the named call would keep only the other fragments.

Nothing shows that any of these happened. The problem is that if one did, today's evidence would look exactly like a model error.

## Expected

For every invalid-arguments event in CI, the evidence says which side broke the JSON:

- The parser message and the assembled arguments (or their head and tail when long) are kept in the diagnostic evidence artifact, not in the score artifact. A message such as `Bad control character in string literal` points to the model; a missing span points to assembly.
- The model client counts, per request, the SSE payloads it skipped as unparseable and the tool-call deltas that had no `index`, and the `[model-arguments]` line includes those counts. A failing request with zero skipped payloads and zero index-less deltas rules out the assembly paths above.

Related: #236 (an invalid call ends the run or subagent) and #233 (the E2E log does not print the run error).

248.author: zy95-12
248.body:
## Background

Following the latest community review, replace the previous L0–L3 proposal with an **L1–L5 testing policy**. The purpose is to separate cheap per-commit validation, post-review functional tests, pre-merge real-model smoke tests, nightly scientific quality monitoring, and full release qualification.

**Current implementation:** [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml) still runs UT / ST / mocked E2E on normal PR updates; [`nightly.yml`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.github/workflows/nightly.yml) and [`release.yml`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml) reuse that workflow. The workflows and branch/merge queue checks must be updated together without dropping existing coverage or release safeguards.

## Target test tiers

| Tier | Trigger / owner | Test scope | Role and expected duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **L1 — Per-Commit Gate** | **Automatic for every new PR commit / head-SHA update** (including initial PR and subsequent pushes) | **Lint + Build** | Fast static/build validation; failed checks block progression |
| **L2 — After-Review Gate** | **After code/design review, an authorized Committer adds the `ready` label to the PR** | **UT + ST + Mock LLM, including mocked E2E** | Validate component and integrated behavior without paid real-model dependency |
| **L3 — Pre-Merge Gate** | **GitHub Merge Queue**, before merging (the `merge_group` event) | **A small set of simple real-LLM end-to-end scenarios** | Minutes-level smoke testing of the actual merge candidate, with bounded runtime and spend |
| **L4 — Nightly Benchmark** | **Scheduled daily** | **Stratified sample of the scientific benchmarks** | Hours-level execution; monitor score/pass-rate movements across a rolling window (e.g. 3 days) |
| **L5 — Release Exit Benchmark** | **Release qualification / exit CI**, unchanged in purpose | **Full benchmark suite scoped to the release** | Complete release-specific validation and reviewable exit report |

### Review / merge flow

1. **Development:** each new PR commit triggers **L1** automatically.
2. **After review:** a **Committer (not the PR author/developer)** applies `ready` to trigger **L2**.
3. **Before merge:** after satisfying the review and L1/L2 policy, the PR enters **Merge Queue**. The queue's `merge_group` candidate triggers **L3**, covering the integrated merge result, not merely an earlier PR head.
4. **After integration:** **L4** runs every day; **L5** runs at release exit.

L1/L2/L3 should be reported as distinct checks. Missing, skipped, or stale required checks must not be treated as a pass.

## Implementation requirements

### 1. L1: automatic per-commit Lint / Build

- Retain `pull_request` creation/reopen and `synchronize` triggers so each PR head-SHA update runs L1 without any manual action; preserve relevant `push` coverage for protected branches. A single push containing multiple commits may produce one check of the resulting head SHA, rather than a separate Actions run for each commit.
- Keep L1 limited to Lint / Build. Remove UT/ST/Mock LLM from the automatic PR policy (they move to L2).
- Make L1 a required, SHA-scoped status check and fail clearly on lint/build errors.

### 2. L2: Committer-controlled `ready` after review

- A **Committer** must review the PR and add the **`ready`** label. The PR author/developer cannot self-authorize this gate.
- On the authorized `ready` label event, execute **UT / ST / Mock LLM**, including existing mocked E2E coverage. **Do not include real-LLM cases in L2**.
- Verify the actor's Committer authorization; do not assume any holder of the label is trusted.
- Bind L2 results to the **exact PR head SHA**. New pushes invalidate earlier L2 approval/results; define an explicit re-review / re-label or controlled rerun mechanism. The queue must not accept stale green results.
- Preserve selected-test accounting, logs, coverage, and diagnostics for this tier.

### 3. L3: simple real-LLM E2E in Merge Queue

- Add a **`merge_group` trigger (typically `checks_requested`)** for the pre-merge real-LLM smoke suite and configure the required check/ruleset so Merge Queue waits for it.
- Check out and test the **merge-group candidate SHA**, including the current base branch and any batched PRs, instead of relying on PR-only results.
- Keep the test selection small, stable, and quick: minimal research workflow, simple tool invocation, basic artifact generation, or equivalent high-value real-model E2E cases. Use explicit timeouts, concurrency limits, retry policy, and LLM-call budget.
- **Security:** a merge-group ref may still contain untrusted PR changes. Do not expose production LLM credentials or privileged tokens to arbitrary checked-out PR code. Use an isolated, least-privilege model execution path, protected credentials and/or a trusted runner/controller design that does not execute untrusted code with those secrets. Define the fork-PR policy explicitly.
- Show which candidate SHA, model configuration, cases and check conclusion were validated; failed, missing, skipped, or timed-out L3 cases must not silently pass.

### 4. L4: daily benchmark sampling and trend tracking

- Run **daily** regardless of whether there is a release in progress.
- Use reproducible **stratified sampling** across scientific task categories/difficulty/risk, with traceable samples and stable comparison cases.
- Record commit SHA, benchmark case ID, model and judge configuration, scores, pass/fail, runtime, and errors.
- Show a rolling comparison (e.g. **3 days**) and distinguish model-gateway failures, evaluation variance, and true regressions.

### 5. L5: release exit / full benchmark

- Trigger during **release qualification** (not for every PR/merge).
- Execute **the full benchmark manifest included in the release scope**, report coverage, pass rates, score deltas, regressions, skipped/quarantined cases, and blockers.
- Preserve the existing binary/Docker build, package smoke, artifact integrity, and release publishing quality gates.

### 6. Preserve existing test architecture

Continue using [`.ci/README.md`](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/main/.ci/README.md), `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`, frozen test plans and `planned == executed == passed` consistency checks. Organize tier-specific profiles/slices without duplicating drifting suites in PR, Merge Queue, Nightly, and Release workflows. Keep coverage and diagnostic evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **L1:** lint and build run automatically on every new PR commit / head update, without a label.
- [ ] **L2:** only an authorized **Committer**, **after review**, can trigger UT / ST / Mock LLM (including mocked E2E) by applying **`ready`**.
- [ ] L2 is bound to the latest PR head SHA; subsequent commits do not inherit stale validation.
- [ ] **L3:** Merge Queue executes the **simple real-LLM E2E suite** for its **merge-group SHA** before allowing merge, with bounded runtime/spend and an enforceable required check.
- [ ] L3 cannot expose secrets to untrusted PR code; no absent/failed/skipped checks are misreported as passes.
- [ ] **L4:** nightly benchmark stratified sampling and approximately three-day trend evidence are available.
- [ ] **L5:** release exit runs the full release-scoped benchmark manifest with a reviewable report.
- [ ] Existing test discovery/accounting, coverage/evidence, binary/Docker/smoke tests, and release integrity remain intact.
- [ ] CI documentation, branch/merge queue rules, and Committer instructions are updated.

## Open design decisions

1. How should a new commit after `ready` invalidate L2 approval? Re-review/re-label or automatically re-run under an explicit authorized policy?
2. How should the repository enforce L2 after-review approval and require it before entering Merge Queue?
3. How should Merge Queue L3 securely access a low-privilege real-LLM endpoint, especially for fork PRs?
4. Which short real-LLM scenarios and time/budget limits qualify for L3, and what are L4 regression thresholds and L5 release sign-off criteria?

Related: [#107 — Community E2E test scenarios](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/issues/107).

cc @zhaozhaozz

251.body:
## What happened

On a developer machine, `pnpm ci:ut` fails one case, and it does so on every run, including on unmodified `main` (`9189206d`):

```text
services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts › a blocked run holds its Session queue until the user decides permission
queued work did not overtake a blocked run in the same Session
2 !== 1
```

After the failure the test process does not exit: the blocked run is cancelled only by the steps after this assertion ([L435-L453](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts#L435-L453)). The same case passes in GitHub Actions. The UT layer runs it under `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh`, so the run goes through JiuwenSwarm.

The second request is not the queued run. Logging the bodies that the test's fake upstream receives shows:

1. A JiuwenSwarm skill-index build, with no tools. For a full build the system prompt starts with "请为全部 Skills 构建一棵便于智能体按用户需求找到目标 Skill 的目录树…"; for an incremental one it is "You rebuild one capability-tree subtree for skill routing. Return one JSON object only."
2. The blocked run's own turn, with the run's 68 tools.

The queued run never sends a request; the queueing itself works.

## Why

1. JiuwenSwarm enables skill retrieval by default (`symphony.skill_retrieval.enabled: true` in its `jiuwenswarm/resources/config.yaml`, tag `workswarm0.2.6`). When a session starts and the instance's skill index (`<instance workspace>/symphony/skill_retrieval`) is missing or stale, Swarm starts a background index build. Its config comment says the build "uses the default configured model".
2. That default model is the adapter's `/llm/default` route, which forwards to `routes.latest()`, "the model of the run that started last and is still going" ([llm_proxy.py L109-L110](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L109-L110), [L415-L425](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/adapter/src/sciencediscovery_adapter/llm_proxy.py#L415-L425)). In this test that is the test's own run, so the build request reaches the test's fake upstream.
3. `startBlockingPermissionGateway` counts every `POST /chat/completions` as a run turn ([L125-L130](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/api/src/run-cancel.test.ts#L125-L130)). When the build request arrives first, it can even satisfy `waitForGatewayTurn(api, 1)`; `gatewayRunCount()` then reads 2 at the assertion.

Whether a build happens depends on the state of the JiuwenSwarm instance, not on the code under test. All rows below are on `main` `9189206d`, with `HOME` pointed at a scratch directory so that the instance is a known one:

| Instance state | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh instance, this test alone | FAIL: build request first |
| Same instance again (index already built) | PASS, one request |
| Fresh instance, whole `run-cancel.test.ts` | 9/9 PASS: the file's first test, "cancelling a queued run…", triggers the build against its own upstream |
| One skill added to the instance, this test alone | FAIL: incremental rebuild request first |
| Full `pnpm ci:ut` with a fresh `HOME` | 3700/3700 PASS |

GitHub runners start each job with a fresh `HOME`, so the file's first test absorbs the build. On a developer machine the instance is `$HOME/.jiuwenswarm-instances/sd-test` (`instance_workspace` in `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh`), shared by every checkout and branch that runs the layer. Branches install different skill sets into it, so its index is often stale when the test session starts.

## Expected

The test checks that the queued run does not start, whatever JiuwenSwarm does in the background:

- Count only requests that belong to the Session's runs, or assert on what the queued run did: its status, and whether any request carries its message ("This must not overtake the blocked run"). Do not assert on the total number of requests to the model endpoint.
- Cancel the blocked run in cleanup even when an assertion fails, so that a failure does not hang the worker.

Optionally, `scripts/with-jiuwenswarm.sh` gives local runs an instance that is not shared with other checkouts, or turns off the background index build for the test instance (`SYMPHONY_SKILL_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED=0`).

## Related behaviour (not in scope here)

`/llm/default` sends every JiuwenSwarm-internal model call (skill-index builds, titles) to whichever run started last. With several sessions running, one session's housekeeping can be served by another session's model and credentials. The gateway already notes this ("The legacy default-model route selects the latest active endpoint, not necessarily the owner of its housekeeping work", [jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts L209-L210](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/9189206dcaf42324501a112414842d294c4d84aa/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts#L209-L210)). It is mentioned here because it is what makes this test sensitive to instance state.
251.title: bug: run-cancel queue test counts JiuwenSwarm's own skill-index build as a second run

252.author: wyhohyw
252.body:
## What happened

The Biomni real E2E currently waits for only the first foreground Run returned by `sendUserMessage`. That Run can become `completed` after it starts a managed background shell Execution. When the Execution finishes, the product delivers its result to the main Agent in a later automatic wake Run. The E2E may check final artifacts and clean up the Session before that wake Run finishes, reporting an incomplete delivery as a failure.

This was observed during local Biomni DA-13-3 and DA-14-1 investigations: the first Run's terminal status was not a reliable signal that the entire request had produced its final answer. The fix is limited to the test harness; the product's separate Run and Execution lifecycles are intentional.

## Expected

- Follow the initial Run, main-Agent background Executions, and subsequent automatic main-Agent wake Runs before asserting final delivery.
- Ignore unrelated subagent Executions and wakes when deciding whether the main request is complete.
- After all observed work is terminal, use a short quiet window to catch a wake Run created just after an Execution finishes.
- On budget expiry, distinguish timeout from a completed run with missing artifacts and cancel active Runs in the Session.
- Cover the settling rules with deterministic unit tests. Keep the existing manual Biomni entry point and quarantine unchanged.

Related: #233 concerns the missing error text in a delivery assertion; this issue concerns checking delivery before the complete Run chain finishes.
